result.topic_en: Latin notes on isothermal surfaces in heat conduction: the cylindrical case, ruling out the case where p, q, r are functions of a single variable, the case of constants (parallel planes), and the start of the general question where the temperature depends on two variables besides time (case n=1), via a quadratic form and its adjugate.
result.transcription:
30.
in quibus $\kappa$ est constans. Hujus ultimae aequationis
integrale completum est:
$\lambda(\beta) = \kappa\sqrt{1+\beta^2} + a + b.\beta$
denotantibus $a, b$ constantes arbitrarias. Inde habemus:
$x + a = -\frac{2\psi(u)\sqrt{u}+\kappa}{\sqrt{1+\beta^2}}$
$y + b = -\frac{(2\psi(u)\sqrt{u}+\kappa)\beta}{\sqrt{1+\beta^2}}$
$(x+a)^2 + (y+b)^2 = [-(2\psi(u)\sqrt{u}+\kappa)^2-] (2\psi(u).\sqrt{u} + \kappa)^2$
Superficies igitur isothermae in hoc casu sunt cylindri
eadem axi {+praediti+} [-gaudentes-]
Casum tertium, in quo $p\,q\,r$ sunt functiones unius
ejusdemque variabilis $\rho$ occurrere {+evenire+} non posse facile
perspicitur. Sit enim:
$p = \psi_1(\rho) \quad q = \psi_2(\rho) \quad r = \psi_3(\rho)$.
Ex aequationibus:
$\frac{\partial q}{\partial z} = \frac{\partial r}{\partial y}\,,\ \frac{\partial r}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial z}\,,\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
sequitur:
$\psi_1'(\rho) : \psi_2'(\rho) : \psi_3'(\rho) = \frac{\partial\rho}{\partial x} : \frac{\partial\rho}{\partial y} : \frac{\partial\rho}{\partial z}$
et aequatio $\Delta = 0$ in hanc transit:
$\psi_1'(\rho)\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial x} + \psi_2'(\rho)\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial y} + \psi_3'(\rho)\frac{\partial\rho}{\partial z} = 0$
quae aequationes sane sunt incompatibiles.
Restat itaque casus quartus, in quo $p, q, r$ sunt constantes
ideoque temperatura constans in planis parallelis.

Quaestionis generalioris, {+quando+} [-quibus casibus-] tempe-
ratura praeter tempus a duabus variabilibus pendere possit,
casum $n = 1$ plane persolvere possumus.
Hoc in casu habetur forma quadratica:
$\begin{pmatrix} c & c & c'' \\ a' & b' & c' \end{pmatrix}$
in qua $a' b'$ sunt functiones lineares ipsius $\gamma$ et $c'$
a $\gamma$ independens; praeterea determinans:
$\begin{vmatrix} c & c' & b' \\ c' & c & a' \\ b' & a' & c \end{vmatrix} = 2a'b'c' - c'c'c'$
constans esse debet. Hujus formae adjuncta haec
est:
$-(a'd\alpha + b'd\beta - c'd\gamma)^2 + 2(2a'b' - cc')\,d\alpha\,d\beta$
in qua $2a'b' - cc'$ a $\gamma$ non pendet. Jam facile perspicitur,
introducendo loco $\gamma$ functionem linearem ipsius $\gamma$
tanquam novam variabilem, illam formam trans-
formari in hanc:
$(a\,d\alpha + c\,d\gamma)^2 + 2m\,d\alpha\,d\beta$
in qua $a$ est functio linearis ipsius $\gamma$, $c$ et $m$ a $\gamma$ non
pendent. Jam conditiones inveniendae sunt, ut haec
forma transformari possit in alteram constantibus coëffi-
cientibus gaudentem {+praeditam+}, sive in formam $dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$

methods.what: Complete integral of the auxiliary ODE in the cylindrical case
Isothermal surfaces are coaxial circular cylinders
Curl-free conditions on the gradient components p, q, r
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial q}{\partial z} = \frac{\partial r}{\partial y}\,,\ \frac{\partial r}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial z}\,,\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$

methods.what: Proportionality of derivatives with grad rho, and the Laplace condition leading to incompatibility
Determinant of the quadratic form must be constant
methods.quote: $\begin{vmatrix} c & c' & b' \\ c' & c & a' \\ b' & a' & c \end{vmatrix} = 2a'b'c' - c'c'c'$

methods.what: Adjugate form of the quadratic form
Normal form after linear change of variable gamma

items.quote:
Superficies igitur isothermae in hoc casu sunt cylindri
eadem axi {+praediti+} [-gaudentes-]
items.english: Therefore the isothermal surfaces in this case are cylinders with the same axis.

items.quote:
Casum tertium, in quo $p\,q\,r$ sunt functiones unius
ejusdemque variabilis $\rho$ occurrere {+evenire+} non posse facile
perspicitur.
items.english: It is easily seen that the third case, in which p, q, r are functions of one and the same variable rho, cannot occur.

items.quote:
Restat itaque casus quartus, in quo $p, q, r$ sunt constantes
ideoque temperatura constans in planis parallelis.
items.english: There remains therefore the fourth case, in which p, q, r are constants and hence the temperature is constant on parallel planes.

items.quote:
Quaestionis generalioris, {+quando+} [-quibus casibus-] tempe-
ratura praeter tempus a duabus variabilibus pendere possit,
casum $n = 1$ plane persolvere possumus.
items.english: Of the more general question, when the temperature can depend, besides time, on two variables, we can completely solve the case n = 1.

items.quote:
Jam conditiones inveniendae sunt, ut haec
forma transformari possit in alteram constantibus coëffi-
cientibus gaudentem {+praeditam+}, sive in formam $dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2$
items.english: Now conditions must be found under which this form can be transformed into another with constant coefficients, or into the form dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2.
